title: Raise A Catboy Eggs: How to Find and Hatch Eggs
description: Learn how eggs work in Raise A Catboy: steal an egg, escape back to your café, hatch a Catboy, and find rarer eggs in later areas.

hero.heading: Raise A Catboy Eggs and Hatching Guide
hero.lead: The confirmed egg loop is: take an egg from Catboys, return safely to your café, and hatch it into a Catboy. The official description also says later areas contain rarer eggs and faster guards.

sections.heading: How to Get Eggs in Raise A Catboy
sections.intro: The public description supports the core sequence, but not a complete egg spawn map, exact controls, or guaranteed routes.

subsections.heading: Steal an egg from Catboys
paragraphs: Egg stealing is a core action in the accessible game description. Treat that as the reliable starting point: the player obtains an egg from Catboys before trying to bring it home.

This guide intentionally does not invent a keybind, interaction radius, respawn timer, egg spawn coordinate, or “best” theft technique. Those details require direct in-game verification before they can be presented as instructions.

subsections.heading: Escape back to your café
paragraphs: The next confirmed task is returning the egg to the café. Later areas are described as more difficult and associated with faster guards, which makes escape part of progression rather than a decorative step.
Because guard AI, routes, and exact speeds were not verified, the safe guidance is to focus on the confirmed objective—get the egg back—without publishing fake route optimization.

sections.heading: How to Hatch Eggs

subsections.heading: What hatching gives you
paragraphs: Once an egg reaches the café, hatching turns it into a Catboy. The confirmed gameplay loop then connects Catboys with earning cash over time, so hatching is the bridge between stealing an egg and growing your economy.
The accessible sources do not establish one universal hatch timer, whether every egg uses the same timing, or exact income values for each result. Those numbers are therefore not shown here.

subsections.heading: What the official listing does not specify
paragraphs: The public game description explains the purpose of eggs at a high level but does not provide a complete odds table, all egg names, or a verified list of hatch percentages.
If a future in-game screen or official post supplies those details, this page should be updated with the source date instead of retrofitting guesses into the current guide.

sections.heading: How to Find Rarer Eggs

subsections.heading: Later areas and faster guards
paragraphs: The confirmed description links later areas with rarer eggs and faster guards. That establishes a progression relationship: rarer egg opportunities are associated with pushing farther into the game.
It does not establish which named rarity belongs to which exact area, how often an egg appears, or a guaranteed route. Any area-by-tier table would be speculative until verified.

subsections.heading: Why Speed training matters
paragraphs: The game description also calls out training Speed on the cat wheel. Combined with the mention of faster guards in later areas, Speed is clearly part of the progression loop.
This page stops short of publishing required Speed thresholds or optimal training breakpoints because no verified values were included in the project evidence.

sections.heading: What Changed in the New Egg System?
sections.intro: The November 2–7 Mutations + QoL announcement included a “New Egg System,” but the accessible announcement did not provide enough detail to reconstruct every mechanic.

subsections.heading: What the announcement confirms
paragraphs: The dated update listing names New Mutations, a New Egg System, New World Events, and Playtime Rewards. For eggs, that confirms that the system was part of the announced update scope.
It does not by itself prove a new drop-rate table, a specific hatch animation, a particular egg inventory interface, or any exact odds.

subsections.heading: What still needs in-game verification
paragraphs: Before this page adds detailed new-system instructions, the implementation should be checked in the live game: how eggs are collected, where they appear, whether the hatch flow changed, and what information the UI actually exposes.
Until then, the reliable player answer remains the confirmed high-level loop rather than a fabricated “complete” system guide.

sections.heading: Common Egg Guide Mistakes to Avoid
paragraphs: Do not confuse a rarity label with a verified hatch probability. The rarity reference can document names such as Common or Divine, but the accessible sources do not publish a complete official odds table.

Do not treat developer-product pricing as a natural egg drop rate, and do not assume an egg associated with a seasonal event uses the same rules as permanent eggs. Those are separate questions that need separate evidence.

Finally, do not copy a map coordinate or “best farming route” unless it has been checked against the current Raise A Catboy experience. Fast-moving Roblox games can change, and a precise-looking route becomes harmful if it points players to outdated content.

faq.question: How do you get eggs in Raise A Catboy?
faq.answer: The confirmed loop is to take an egg from Catboys and get it safely back to your café. Exact controls, spawn coordinates, and guaranteed routes are not established in the sources used for this guide.

faq.question: How do you hatch eggs in Raise A Catboy?
faq.answer: The public gameplay description says eggs are brought back to the café and hatched into Catboys. It does not establish a universal hatch timer or exact hatch odds.

faq.question: Where are rarer eggs?
faq.answer: The official-style game description says later areas contain rarer eggs and faster guards. A verified area-by-rarity map was not available, so this guide does not invent one.

subsections.heading: Source and date of the rarity list
paragraphs: The project research captured eleven names from a third-party reference that traced the labels to Roblox developer products on November 3, 2026. That makes the labels useful as a documented snapshot.
Direct live product-API revalidation was not available in the handoff, so this page attaches the date to the list and does not present old prices or assume the list can never change.

subsections.heading: How we order the labels
paragraphs: The recorded list is presented in the same broad sequence used by the captured reference: Common through Divine. The highest-priced “Steal” product label in that snapshot was Divine.

Price order is not the same thing as official hatch probability, combat power, income, or a formal developer-published rarity hierarchy. The page therefore calls these documented labels rather than an official odds ranking.

sections.heading: Do Rarity Names Reveal Drop Rates?

subsections.heading: No official hatch percentages
paragraphs: No official probability table was established in the accessible project evidence. A label such as Divine or Secret may communicate scarcity, but it does not tell us a verified percentage chance.
For that reason, this guide does not invent values such as “1%” or “0.1%,” and it does not copy unsourced community percentages into a table.

subsections.heading: Pricing is not probability or power
paragraphs: Developer-product pricing can be evidence that a label exists, but it cannot independently prove how often a result appears from normal gameplay. It also does not prove how much cash a Catboy earns or whether one result is always stronger than another.
A future direct in-game rarity panel, official odds notice, or developer statement would be stronger evidence for those questions. Until then, price and probability stay separate.

sections.heading: How Rarer Eggs Relate to Progression

subsections.heading: Later areas and Speed
paragraphs: The confirmed game description says players can reach later areas with rarer eggs and faster guards, while the cat wheel is used to train Speed. That establishes a real progression connection between movement capability, harder areas, and rarer egg opportunities.
It does not establish an exact “Common in Zone 1, Rare in Zone 2” mapping, so this page avoids a tier-to-area chart without direct evidence.

subsections.heading: Egg acquisition vs. rarity label
paragraphs: The egg page answers how the acquisition and hatch loop works. This rarity page answers what labels have been documented and what those labels do—or do not—prove.
Keeping those tasks separate prevents a player looking for a rarity reference from having to read an entire stealing tutorial, while also avoiding duplicate pages for every keyword variation.

subsections.heading: What rarity describes
paragraphs: Rarity labels are documented category names associated with Catboy-related developer products in the captured source. They are useful as classification terms, but their exact gameplay math remains unverified in the evidence package.

subsections.heading: What the Mutation update announced
paragraphs: The November Mutations + QoL announcement separately named “New Mutations.” Because the announcement did not publish verified mutation names or effects in the accessible evidence, mutations are treated as a different system and maintained on their own page.

subsections.heading: Source log and new labels
paragraphs: A new label should be added only when it is visible in a current Roblox developer product, an official post, or direct in-game evidence that can be dated. A third-party list can point to a candidate, but it should not silently become a permanent fact without a source trail.

subsections.heading: When to revise an entry
paragraphs: If a developer product disappears, is renamed, or a live in-game rarity panel provides a different set, the page should record the newer evidence and review date. Historical prices should not be kept as if they are current unless they are directly rechecked.

faq.question: How many rarities are in Raise A Catboy?
faq.answer: Eleven names were identifiable in the November 3 developer-product-based snapshot used for this project. Because direct live revalidation was not completed, this guide treats the count as a dated documented list rather than an eternal official total.

faq.question: What is the rarest Catboy?
faq.answer: Divine was the highest-priced Steal label in the captured developer-product list. That is not proof of the rarest natural hatch odds, so this guide does not convert price order into a probability claim.

faq.question: What is the drop chance of Divine?
faq.answer: No official Divine hatch probability was established in the accessible sources, so no percentage is published here.

hero.heading: Raise A Catboy Mutations Update
hero.lead: The November 2–7, 2026 “MUTATIONS + QoL Update” announcement listed New Mutations, a New Egg System, New World Events, and Playtime Rewards. The available evidence does not verify individual mutation names, effects, odds, or obtain methods.

sections.heading: What the Raise A Catboy Mutations Update Announced
sections.intro: This page is announcement-first: it records what the dated listing actually named and separates that from mechanics that still require live verification.

table.caption: Features named in the November 2–7, 2026 Mutations + QoL announcement

The listing names new world events.

subsections.heading: Source and update window
paragraphs: The project handoff records a Roblox virtual-event digest for November 2 through November 7, 2026 under the title “MUTATIONS + QoL Update.” The accessible evidence came through a dated reference rather than a direct live Roblox event-page read.
That means the announcement scope is useful, but effect-level claims still need first-party or in-game confirmation before publication.

subsections.heading: Why this is not a full mutation list yet
paragraphs: The word “Mutations” in an announcement does not supply the names or properties of every mutation. Publishing a complete-looking list without evidence would be more misleading than leaving a clearly labeled verification gap.
This page therefore answers the real current question—what was announced—and is designed to accept verified mutation entries later without changing the URL or search intent.

sections.heading: How Do Mutations Work in Raise A Catboy?

subsections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: A mutation system was explicitly named in the dated update announcement. That is enough to establish that mutations are a real game topic and a distinct player task from rarity labels or Thanksgiving event content.
The project evidence does not establish whether mutations alter income, appearance, rarity, movement, hatch odds, or some other property. Those effects remain unverified.

subsections.heading: What still needs in-game proof
paragraphs: A reliable mechanics section needs direct observations or an official explanation showing mutation names, how players obtain them, what each one changes, whether effects stack, and whether the system has probabilities.
Until that evidence exists, this guide avoids plausible-sounding mechanics and instead tells players exactly which details are still awaiting confirmation.

sections.heading: How the Mutation Update Relates to the New Egg System

subsections.heading: Two announced systems in one update
paragraphs: The same dated update listing named both New Mutations and a New Egg System. That makes it reasonable to discuss them together as parts of the same update window, but it does not prove a specific cause-and-effect relationship between mutations and hatching.

subsections.heading: Keep egg instructions on the egg page
paragraphs: The dedicated egg guide covers the confirmed steal → return → hatch loop and later-area progression. This page only records the new-system announcement so the two URLs do not compete by repeating the same tutorial.

links.label: Raise A Catboy eggs
links.description: Use the egg guide for acquisition, hatching, and progression details that are actually verified.

sections.heading: New World Events and Playtime Rewards

subsections.heading: World events were announced
paragraphs: “New World Events” appears in the update scope recorded by the project research. No verified rotation timetable, event trigger, reward table, or named event list was included in the accessible evidence.

subsections.heading: Playtime rewards were announced
paragraphs: “Playtime Rewards” was also named. Without a direct in-game reward screen, this page does not publish time thresholds, item names, or quantities. Those are high-change details that should be copied only from current evidence.

sections.heading: Mutation Verification Checklist
bullets: Confirm a mutation name from a current in-game screen or first-party source.
Record how the mutation is obtained before writing a step-by-step method.
Record the exact effect and any visible numeric modifier only when directly shown.
Keep rarity labels separate unless a first-party source explicitly connects rarity and mutation mechanics.
Update the review date when verified mechanics replace announcement-only wording.

sections.heading: Mutations vs. Rarities: Keep the Systems Separate
paragraphs: The project evidence supports both a documented rarity-label set and a separately announced mutation system. It does not establish that every rarity has a matching mutation, that mutations change rarity, or that one system determines the odds of the other.

For players, that means the rarity page is the right place to check documented category names, while this page is the right place to track mutation mechanics once effects and obtain methods can be verified. Separating the tasks also prevents one page from repeating the same keywords and claims as another.

sections.heading: How This Mutation Guide Will Be Updated
paragraphs: When direct evidence becomes available, new mutation information should be added in a fixed order: name, source date, obtain method, observable effect, and any numeric value that the game actually displays. If only a community claim exists, it should remain outside the confirmed table until independently checked.

If the developer changes or removes a mutation, the page should update the current guidance rather than silently preserving an old effect as evergreen truth. The last-reviewed date should move only when the underlying facts are actually rechecked.

faq.answer: A verified complete mutation list was not available in the project evidence, so this page does not invent names or copy unsourced lists.
